description: Low-rank PR-routing is the run's PROVEN winner (shapes 3/4/8/10/12). brief-11 just made the inner k-by-k Rayleigh eigh cheap (raw megakernel), which shifts the low-rank path's bottleneck to its OUTER cost: the randomized subspace iteration's CholeskyQR2 (Gram Q^T Q GEMM + triangular solve) and the range-finder GEMMs, most of which still run FP32-SIMT. Deepen the proven path (distinct from brief-11's inner-solve work and brief-7's gate/A@X precision work): (1) route the CholeskyQR2 Gram Q^T Q and the subspace projection GEMMs through TF32/FP16 tensor cores under the loose gate (brief-6 measured TF32 8-10x FP32-SIMT at relerr 2.9e-4 << 1.2% gate), keeping only the final orthonormalization in FP32; (2) RE-TUNE k downward now that a cheaper inner solve changes the k-vs-accuracy tradeoff (smaller k = smaller complement + cheaper CQR2, and the residual gate catches under-resolved matrices); (3) re-sweep the per-n PR-band routing table to capture any dense shapes currently just outside the bands. Per-matrix residual-gated cuSOLVER fallback unchanged; forks best 12251fe so wins stack. -O2 for any load_inline; no 'stream' substring; do not regress the megakernel shapes 1/2.

t1: route CholeskyQR2 Gram Q^T Q through TF32 (all CQR2 calls). MEASURED REGRESSION: geomean 41396->49081. TF32 Gram breaks orthonormalization -> per-matrix orth gate fails, low-rank shapes 3/4/8/10/12 fall back to full cuSOLVER (~2x): shape3 109727->139188, shape4 83912->150972, shape8 120979->141901, shape10 105006->164446, shape12 46613->101516. CQR2 2nd pass does not absorb TF32 ~3e-4 error.

t2: range-finder CQR2 -> 1 pass (power step re-orthonormalizes; final power CQR2 kept 2-pass). Probed 0 fallback, orth<=1.7e-3. geomean 41396->40921 (~1.1%): shape3 109727->101994 (7%), shape4 83912->80028 (4.6%), shape8 120979->117963 (2.5%), shape12 46613->44443 (4.7%); shape10 105006->110619 (nearrank exact-rank slightly worse). Reset tf32_gram default False. FINDING: dom-subspace CQR2 (ill-cond Qd) MUST stay FP32 (t1); only well-cond complement Gram can be TF32.

t3: complement CQR2 Gram -> TF32 (well-cond complement; projections FP32). Stacks on t2. geomean 40921->40400 (~1.3%, 2.4% over parent 41378): shape3 101994->100391, shape4 80028->77895, shape8 117963->117037, shape10 110619->109882, shape12 44443->39965 (largest complement nc=640 benefits most). Validated 39/39.

t4: 3xTF32 (Ozaki hi+lo split, 3 TF32 bmms) Gram for both dominant+complement CQR2. Numerically SAFE (orth<=8.5e-3, 0 fallback on shapes 3/4/10/12). MEASURED REGRESSION vs t3: geomean 40400->41459 (clean, 2 runs). ROOT CAUSE: trsm (not Gram) dominates CQR2 (~16% profile); 3xTF32 split overhead (int32 mask + 3 bmms + 2 adds on B*n*k tensors) exceeds small Gram savings, esp b640/n=512: shape3 100391->124579, shape8 117037->135516. Neutral n=1024. FINDING: outer-Gram precision is NOT the lever; the CQR2 triangular solve is.

t5: dominant Gram back to FP32 (t4 3xTF32 net-lost); complement final CQR -> 1-pass. geomean 41315 (2 clean runs), WORSE than t3 40400. shape3 98373/shape4 76107/shape10 108620 improved but shape8 135644 + shape12 48461 REGRESS (complement 1-pass raises fallbacks on rankdef512/lapgeom1024 live; isolated probe under-counted). Net loss. Best remains t3 40400 (dom-fp32 + comp-tf32-2pass + range-1pass).

t6: restore t3 winning config (dominant Gram FP32 + complement Gram TF32 2-pass + range-finder 1-pass). CONFIRMED BEST: geomean 40390-40413 (2 clean runs, reproduces t3 40400 = 2.4% over parent 41378). shape3 100480, shape4 77882, shape8 117147, shape10 109833, shape12 39819. Clean base for further work.

t7: complement Gram -> 3xTF32. MEASURED REGRESSION vs t6: geomean 40390->41152. 3xTF32 split overhead net-loses even on smaller nc complement Gram, esp b640: shape8 117147->138485, shape12 39819->41493. Confirms t4 across the board: 3xTF32 overhead > Gram savings. Best remains t6 (complement plain TF32) 40390.

t8: orthogonality-gate V^T V GEMM -> 3xTF32 (Ozaki split). This n*n*n batched GEMM is a large FP32-SIMT term (~4ms shape3 b640); 3xTF32 is ~FP32-accurate (0 gate-decision disagreements) and ~1.6x faster as a SINGLE one-shot GEMM (beats FP32-SIMT here, unlike inside trsm-dominated CQR2 loop; plain TF32 unsafe - inflates orth, flips ~640 decisions). Stacks on t6. geomean 40390->40264 (2 clean runs), all low-rank shapes improve (s3 99552 s4 76839 s8 116296 s10 108596 s12 38804). NEW BEST = 2.76% over parent 41378.

t9: Vd lift + complement projections -> 3xTF32 (both well-cond, one-shot GEMMs). Numerically safe (Vd matches FP32 orth exactly). geomean 40272-40292, NEUTRAL vs t8 40264: n=1024 slightly better (s4 76040, s12 38582), b640 worse (s8 118366) -- 3xTF32 split overhead offsets gain at high batch; these GEMMs smaller than the gate V^TV where 3xTF32 won. Net wash. Best t8 40264.

Deepened the low-rank OUTER path. NEW BEST HEAD 334d60a1 (submission.py byte-identical to 7eb7a5d16), geomean ~40247us = 2.78% over parent 41378 (12251fe), idle-stable across 4 clean runs (40228-40305), 39/39 validate, banned-'stream'-clean, diff vs parent = submission.py only (+88/-11). THREE STACKING WINS, all on the low-rank shapes 3/4/8/10/12: (1) range-finder CQR2 -> 1 pass (the power step re-orthonormalizes, so the intermediate basis need not be gate-orthonormal; 0 fallback, ~5-8% per shape) [t2]; (2) complement CQR2 Gram -> plain TF32 (the complement is WELL-conditioned so its Gram tolerates TF32; ~9x off the FP32-SIMT path, 0-1 fallback) [t3]; (3) orthogonality-GATE V^T V GEMM -> 3xTF32 Ozaki hi+lo split (~FP32-accurate: 0 gate-decision disagreements vs FP32; ~1.6x faster because it's a big SINGLE one-shot n*n*n GEMM where the 3-GEMM cost still beats FP32-SIMT) [t8].

KEY MEASURED NEGATIVES (refuting brief hypotheses, so the manager can steer elsewhere): (a) TF32 on the DOMINANT CQR2 Gram is UNSAFE -- Qd is ill-conditioned (kappa 1e3-1e4 by construction of a concentrated spectrum), so TF32's 3e-4 error blows orth to 0.1-1.3 >> gate -> ~100% cuSOLVER fallback (t1, +19% geomean). Even mixed pass1-FP32/pass2-TF32 fails. (b) 3xTF32 on the dominant Gram / Vd lift / complement projections is numerically SAFE but net-NEUTRAL-to-LOSS (t4/t7/t9): the CQR2 trsm (not the Gram) dominates CQR2 (~9-13% profile), and the Ozaki split overhead (int32 mask + 3 bmms + 2 adds on B*n*k) exceeds the small Gram savings, ESPECIALLY at b640/n=512 (shapes 3/8). 3xTF32 only wins on the ONE large one-shot GEMM (the gate). (c) k RE-TUNING DOWNWARD is BLOCKED: k is already at the eigen-residual floor for every shape (shape4 needs k=608 or eig-resid 5e-2>>1.8e-2 gate; shape3 k=352, shape12 k=384 all at floor; k-1 band -> 100% fallback). The inner-solve cost was never what set k -- the spectral TAIL sets it -- so a cheaper inner solve doesn't lower k. Power=2/3 doesn't help (tail-limited, not subspace-limited). (d) BAND RE-SWEEP captures NO new shapes: lapeven512 (shape11, PR=284 homogeneous) gives low-rank eig-resid 0.27 at k=448 (flat spectrum, un-winnable); mixed512/1024 (shapes 6/7) are heterogeneous (max/min PR ~19-20) so the homogeneity gate correctly excludes them.

OPEN DIRECTIONS I did NOT reach: (1) the CQR2 TRIANGULAR SOLVE (batch_trsm_left, ~9-13% of every low-rank shape, the single biggest OUTER op) is intrinsic FP32 and resisted every precision trick -- a structurally different orthonormalizer (e.g. a fused Newton-Schulz that keeps the ill-conditioned dominant subspace orthonormal, or a batched-trsm kernel that engages more SMs) is untouched. (2) On shape4 (dense1024, k=608) and shape10 (nearrank, k=768) the INNER reduced eigh STILL runs cuSOLVER (laed3/sytrd/laed4 visible in the final profile) because k>448 overflows the megakernel's SMEM -- a k>448 batched dense solver (out-of-SMEM-tiled megakernel or batched TC reduction) would move those two shapes' inner solve to tensor cores (this is brief-11 territory but the k>448 case was explicitly left open there). (3) The final gate's eig-residual + the sort/gather at the end of _lowrank_eigh are elementwise/memory-bound and unprofiled as a lever.
